scenes.tts: In March 1948 Pauling was on his back in Oxford with a sinus infection, reading mystery novels until they bored him. Then he asked his wife to bring him paper and a slide rule.
scenes.visual: portrait inset; dated timeline March 1948, Oxford, sinus infection, novels, paper + slide rule
scenes.narration: In March 1948 Pauling was on his back in Oxford with a sinus infection, reading mystery novels until they bored him. Then he asked his wife to bring him paper and a slide rule.

scenes.tts: He drew a polypeptide chain at the right scale, kept every peptide bond flat the way the chemistry demanded, and folded the strip until it wound onto itself — a right-handed coil, 3.6 residues per turn, every backbone NH hydrogen-bonded to a CO four residues back.
scenes.visual: strip of residue tiles winds into end-on coil; 3.6 per turn; NH to CO four back
scenes.narration: He drew a polypeptide chain at the right scale, kept every peptide bond flat the way the chemistry demanded, and folded the strip until it wound onto itself — a right-handed coil, 3.6 residues per turn, every backbone NH hydrogen-bonded to a CO four residues back.

scenes.tts: He noticed the rise per turn came out near 5.4 angstroms, not quite the 5.1 measured for keratin, and let the discrepancy stand rather than bend the chemistry to fit it.
scenes.visual: bar compare 5.4 vs 5.1 angstrom, discrepancy left standing
scenes.narration: He noticed the rise per turn came out near 5.4 angstroms, not quite the 5.1 measured for keratin, and let the discrepancy stand rather than bend the chemistry to fit it.

scenes.tts: He had taught the world to deduce a structure from the bonds alone — and four years later the State Department refused to renew his passport, keeping him out of London where the DNA photographs waited. The man who could read structure from first principles missed the structure of the gene.
